reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because its speakers promote mining participation and package sales through a downline while presenting early entry as an opportunity to make a fortune. They use a time-limited split benefit, future-value comparisons, claimed difficulty increases, and recruitment-linked price claims to encourage participation.

button, I will receive 3 One Coins for this.
By actually selling a package to a new or existing downline, you will mine the coin directly.
the more people who start mining the one coin, the higher the price of the coin in the market.
The more people come in the more valuable your coins become.

opening.argument: The presentation does not frame participation as an automatic or guaranteed result. It explicitly leaves the decision with the audience: “it is your decision what you want to do with your tokens,” and ties strategy to what viewers believe about the company and coin. It also invites questions after the presentation and says the webinar will be recorded for later review, which is consistent with an open informational discussion rather than a concealed solicitation. The speakers present competing choices, including mining or selling, rather than insisting on one inevitable outcome.

citations.quote: it is your decision what you want to do with your tokens
what you believe about the company, what you believe about the coin should actually make your strategy up
yes, there will be questions and answers after.
this will be recorded by that will be able to review it on YouTube and our Facebook channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing reading emphasizes promotional language but overlooks the explicit qualification that the decision belongs to the viewer. A comparison of mining and selling is not itself a guarantee, and the invitation to ask questions and review the recording makes the format more transparent. The excerpts do not show a promise that every participant will profit or that loss is impossible.

citations.quote: it is your decision what you want to do with your tokens
yes, there will be questions and answers after.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the decision voluntary does not remove the solicitation. The same presentation compares a package cost with projected coin proceeds and says mining should begin before a stated deadline. Its strongest language is not merely conditional analysis: viewers are told “please do so,” that “everybody needs to be mining,” and that they should bring people into the opportunity. A Q&A format can still promote paid participation.

citations.quote: I would say yes, please do so, because in 4 weeks the mining's difficulty will go up
Everybody needs to be mining.
make sure to bring as many people as you can into this opportunity

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be understood as an educational webinar explaining how a new digital-currency system is supposed to work. The presenter says the purpose is to discuss “how we mined the coin” and explain the technical side so participants can handle questions. The slides address mining mechanics, dashboards, account splits, blockchain activity, and frequently asked questions. That instructional structure matters: discussing a system's proposed operation, comparing it with Bitcoin, and answering technical questions is not the same as proving or selling a deceptive outcome.

citations.quote: i would like to talk to you today about how we mined the coin a bit on technical side
So you understand what it's all about and also you can brief your downlines and can handle all the questions.
How many OneCoins have been mined you can always check on the website.
What does the blockchain show

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing side treats every explanation of mining as an offer, but the recorded content spends substantial time describing technical mechanics and responding to frequently asked questions. References to a dashboard, blockchain, mining difficulty, and account rules support an operational demonstration. Promotional tone may accompany educational content without changing its central subject into a proven scam.

citations.quote: How many OneCoins have been mined you can always check on the website.
What does the blockchain show
we have been constantly collecting frequently asked questions from all of you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical framing is part of the pitch, not a neutral tutorial. The speaker expressly says the explanation will help viewers brief their “downlines,” while another speaker says selling a package to a downline mines the coin directly. The webinar then directs the audience to build its network and bring package buyers in. Technical vocabulary does not erase the paid recruitment mechanism.

By actually selling a package to a new or existing downline, you will mine the coin directly.
We do that by attracting new miners into the business

opening.argument: The supplied material does not show a completed payment, a submitted order, an account transfer, or a guaranteed payout. What it does show is discussion of a digital-currency service, mining settings, token allocation, and alternative user choices. The presentation even describes a company-operated pool distributing coins to customer wallets and explains that transactions are currently limited. Those details fit a proposed commercial platform or service demonstration. The record alone does not establish that a viewer deposited money and received a promised return, so the more severe interpretation requires assumptions beyond the supplied evidence.

citations.quote: We built the pool and the company mine, and we distribute some the coins.
the company mine in the company wallet and then distributes to the wallets of the customers.
currently we do not have transactions or not many

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a visible checkout or completed payout does not make the presentation something other than ordinary promotion. It discusses a service, its mining process, and alternatives such as selling or mining. The supplied frames show dashboards and FAQs rather than a payment confirmation. Interpreting an offer as deceptive would require facts the record does not establish, including an actual loss or a fabricated transaction.

citations.quote: currently we do not have transactions or not many
We built the pool and the company mine, and we distribute some the coins.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed payment is not required when the video itself promotes paid entry. It says viewers paid for packages, compares the package price with expected coin amounts, and instructs them to sell packages to downlines. It also creates urgency through an end-of-May mining promotion and claims that recruiting more miners raises coin value. Those statements describe the mechanism being solicited, even if the sampled frames do not show a checkout screen.
